item.name: The Big Sky
entries: {@i The Big Sky} represents widespread change or liberation. As long as you have {@i The Big Sky} invested, you gain a +2 item bonus to {@skill Perception} checks made while you are flying outside during the day and to any check made to {@action Escape}. The bonus increases to +3 if you are at least 17th level.

For 10 minutes, you and up to four creatures you touch ignore difficult terrain and effects that would give a circumstance penalty to Speed. If you are at least 17th level, the targets also ignore greater difficult terrain.

footers.name: Epitome
entries: When you epitomize {@i The Big Sky}, assign it to a point of interest in the {@plane The Harrow Court|SF1|Harrow Court's} desert area. This marks the location of a sprawling expanse of sand that's been melted into a field of reflective glass that mirrors the sky above. The temperature here during the day is extreme heat—every 10 minutes, a creature in the region takes {@damage 2d6} fire damage. At night, the reverse holds true; the temperate here becomes extremely cold and inflicts {@damage 2d6} cold damage every 10 minutes. More astonishingly, this region has a supernatural ability to help a creature use their raw strength to break free from {@trait curse||curses} they're suffering from. Once per day, a character can spend an hour meditating here, enduring either the extreme heat or cold, but at the end of that hour, the character can select one {@trait curse} that they're currently afflicted by, then attempt an {@skill Athletics} check against the {@trait curse||curse's} DC.

Success: The {@trait curse} is counteracted as long as its level is equal to or less than the character's level.
Failure: The {@trait curse} is counteracted as long as its level is equal to or less than the character's level – 4.
Critical Failure: The {@trait curse} is not removed, and the character overextends themselves in the attempt, becoming {@condition enfeebled||enfeebled 3}.

item.name: The Brass Dwarf
entries: {@i The Brass Dwarf} represents invulnerability. When you invest {@i The Brass Dwarf}, you gain resistance to fire equal to your level.

Choose acid, cold, electricity, fire, {@i mental}, poison, or sonic. You can't choose the damage type for which {@i The Brass Dwarf} currently gives you resistance. You gain resistance to the damage you chose equal to your level, and you lose the prior resistance that {@i The Brass Dwarf} gave you. For 1 minute, you gain weakness equal to half your level to the damage type of the prior resistance.

footers.name: Epitome
entries: A clockwork dwarf made of brass manifests in one of Harrowheart's workshops. The brass dwarf's presence and assistance increases the item bonus granted to {@skill Crafting} checks in the workshop to +2. The brass dwarf has no name, but gracefully accepts any the PCs offer them. The brass dwarf knows the formulas for all {@item armor potency (generic)||armor potency} runes, {@item resilient (generic)||resilient potency} runes, {@item energy-resistant (generic)||energy-resistant} runes, and {@item fortification (generic)||fortification} runes—they can teach these formulas to the PCs.

item.name: The Carnival
entries: {@i The Carnival} represents false dreams. When you have {@i The Carnival} invested, your flat check DCs to obtain reliable information from {@trait divination} effects (such as {@spell augury} or {@spell read fate}, or the activation of this card) are reduced by 2 (but not to less than 2). Casting a {@trait divination} effect with a flat check, whether or not the flat check succeeds, gives a series of subtly different visions that don't confuse the meaning but make you stupefied 1 for 1 round. If you're at least 17th level, the flat check is instead reduced by 3.

You peer into the future and witness yourself walking through a colorful but vaguely sinister carnival, meeting a variety of strange people. One of these people looks more genuine than the others and resembles someone you're likely to meet for the first time in the next 24 hours (if anyone). This resemblance might be metaphorical, such a clown signifying someone who is silly or a stilt-walker representing someone who is tall. You also get a sense for whether this person can be trusted, should be distrusted, or neither, based on how they're most likely to interact with you and your allies. The GM decides who this new person might be, then rolls a secret DC {@flatDC 6} flat check. On a failure, the result is always "neither," making it hard to determine whether a "neither" result is accurate.

footers.name: Epitome
entries: When you epitomize {@i The Carnival}, assign it to a point of interest in the {@plane The Harrow Court|SF1|Harrow Court's} farmland area. This marks the location of a colorful, vibrant, and slightly off-putting fairground where festivals and celebrations are in constant swing. The simulacra who inhabit this carnival never leave and tend to subtly draw appearances and themes from potential foes the PC may face in their future. Once per week, a character can spend 8 hours at the fairground simply observing its participants—those who do can attempt a DC 28 {@skill Perception} check.

entries.Critical Success: The PC observes some of the carnival performers and gains subtle clues as to the nature of a foe they will soon face. The GM chooses a specific, named enemy that the PCs are likely to face at some point in the current adventure they're playing. When the PC encounters that foe (as long as the foe isn't disguised), they automatically recognize them. At this point, the GM informs the PC that they recognize the foe from their visit to the carnival, and the PC learns information about the foe as if they had achieved a critical success in an attempt to {@action Recall Knowledge} against that target. Until the party encounters and defeats that foe, they cannot visit this carnival again to search for clues.
entries.Success: As success, but instead of granting insight into the nature of a specific foe, the GM chooses a generic monster that the PCs may soon face, selecting from standard monsters that might be encountered in the current adventure the PCs are playing. The information gained is equal to what the PC would have gained from a success by {@action Recall Knowledge||Recalling Knowledge} about that monster.
entries.Failure: Apart from a vaguely unsettling feeling of being watched themselves, the PC learns nothing from their visit to the carnival.
entries.Critical Failure: Rather than noticing anything helpful, the PC emerges from their trip to the carnival with paranoid feelings of being watched by unseen eyes, and becomes {@condition stupefied||stupefied 3}.

item.name: The Empty Throne
entries: Suit Crown (Cha); Alignment lawful good The Empty Throne represents great loss and wisdom from those who are now gone. As long as you have The Empty Throne invested, it grants you a +2 item bonus to {@skill Society} and {@skill Lore} checks made to {@action Recall Knowledge} regarding individuals who are no longer alive (such as checks to learn about Taldor's historical founder, but not to learn about its current empress). This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.
You overwhelm a target you can see within 60 feet with feelings of helplessness and loss. The creature must attempt a Will DC equal to your class DC.

Critical Success: Once during the next month, you can reroll a failed or critically failed saving throw. This is a {@trait fortune} effect.
Success: As critical success, but you can only reroll a failed saving throw. This is a {@trait fortune} effect.
Failure: You gain no benefit from the meditation.
Critical Failure: The next time you critically succeed at a significant or important saving throw, as determined by the GM, you must reroll that saving throw. This is a {@trait misfortune} effect.

item.name: The Fiend
entries: {@i The Fiend} represents the inevitability of great calamities and pervasive dangers. As long as you have {@i The Fiend} invested, when you repeat a non-{@action Strike} action you previously took in the same round, you gain a +2 item bonus to checks to perform that action. This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.

You wave the card to create a vision of destruction around you; you cast {@spell phantasmal calamity}, except the area is a 20-foot emanation. The level of the spell is one-half your level, rounded down (minimum 6th level), and the save DC is your class DC. You are immune to the effects of your own phantasmal calamity.

footers.name: Epitome
entries: A new room manifests in Harrowheart—a conjuration chamber. Books and tomes stored in this room contain all the information needed to learn the rituals of {@ritual planar ally} and {@ritual planar binding}, and inscriptions carved into the floor of the conjuration chamber grant a +2 item bonus to skill checks made to perform either of these rituals. This increases to a +3 item bonus if the creature being conjured is a {@trait fiend}.

item.name: The Juggler
entries: {@i The Juggler} represents coordination and destiny. As long as you have {@i The Juggler} invested and you aren't carrying an item in two hands, you have a free hand (as you keep tossing the items in your hands back and forth, keeping one in the air at all times). You can use all items in your hands normally, so long as they can be used or wielded in one hand. If you can't act while you're carrying more items than your actual number of hands, you release all items you're holding or wielding. If you are at least 17th level, you instead have two free hands, as you can juggle an additional item.

entries.trigger: an item of 1 Bulk or less falls within your reach, or an attacker fails an attack roll to hit you or a creature within your reach with a thrown weapon of 1 Bulk or less
entries: You grab the triggering item. If all of your hands are full (including any extra free hands from {@i The Juggler}), you must immediately release an item, which can include the triggering item.

footers.name: Epitome
entries: When {@i The Juggler} is epitomized into {@plane the Harrow Court|SF1}, a town square manifests in the village surrounding Harrowheart. Simulacra jugglers, as well as other types of street performers, can be counted on for entertainment at all times in the town square. A PC can spend 8 hours interacting with these entertainers to adjust their methods to match entertainment styles common to a specific city that they're familiar with by attempting a DC 30 {@skill Performance} check. On a success, the entertainers take up that style, and as long as they continue performing in that city's style, a PC can use the {@action Enter the Harrow Court|SF1} activity to open a one-way portal to a marketplace in that city. Switching to a new city requires another successful DC 30 {@skill Performance} check and familiarity with that city.

item.name: The Liar
entries: {@i The Liar} represents obsession or treacherous love. As long as you have {@i The Liar} invested, it grants you a +2 item bonus to {@skill Deception} checks to {@action Lie}. This increases to a +3 item bonus if you're at least 17th level. If the implausibility of your lies prompts a circumstance penalty to your {@skill Deception} checks or an increase to your {@skill Deception} DC, reduce that penalty or increase by half.

You touch a weapon and instill faithlessness within it. The weapon gains the {@item backbiting|GMG} {@trait curse}. The {@trait curse} lasts until you use this activation again. If you're at least 17th level, you can instead use this activation on a weapon within 30 feet. If the weapon is carried by a creature, it can resist the effect with a successful Will save against your class DC.

footers.name: Epitome
entries: A liar moves in to the village surrounding Harrowheart, but this shifty simulacrum has little interest in deceiving the PCs. In fact, they eagerly offer their aid in the deceptive arts. A character who visits the liar's home can take advantage of their expertise and tools—doing so grants a +2 item bonus to checks made to {@action Create Forgery||Create Forgeries} or to assume a disguise with {@action Impersonate}. The liar also knows how to cast the {@trait uncommon} spells {@spell discern lies}, {@spell glibness}, and {@spell zone of truth}, and can teach these spells to PCs.

item.name: The Locksmith
entries: {@i The Locksmith} represents opening locks, including metaphorical locks such as unlocking fate. As long as you have {@i The Locksmith} invested, it grants you a +2 item bonus to {@skill Thievery} checks to {@action Pick a Lock}. This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.

entries.trigger: You would be afflicted by a {@trait curse} or a {@trait disease}
entries: You mimic the turning of a key in a lock and free yourself from your unpleasant fate. You attempt to counteract the triggering affliction, using half your level (rounded up) as the counteract level and a counteract check modifier equal to your class DC − 10.

footers.name: Epitome
entries: A talented if somewhat shady locksmith moves into the village surrounding Harrowheart. This simulacrum is nameless, and the building they bring to the village is more akin to a strange museum of obscure and unusual locks and keys (none of which, of course, have any use beyond being strange displays). Their equipment can't be removed from the museum, but PCs who bring devices and locks to this building can take advantage of their tools to gain a +2 item bonus to checks made to {@action Disable a Device} or {@action Pick a Lock}. The locksmith knows the formulas for how to create {@item chime of opening||chimes of opening}, {@item keymaking tools|SoM}, {@item ring of maniacal devices||rings of maniacal devices}, {@item skeleton key (generic)||skeleton keys}, {@item traveler's any-tool||traveler's any-tools}, and any other lock- or puzzle-themed magic item you might wish to include, and can teach these formulas to the PCs. Characters who use the locksmith's gear to craft such items gain a +2 item bonus on {@skill Crafting} checks.

item.name: The Mountain Man
entries: {@i The Mountain Man} represents creatures with incredible physical power. As long as you have {@i The Mountain Man} invested, it grants you a +2 item bonus to {@skill Athletics} checks to {@action Force Open}, {@action Grapple}, {@action Shove}, or {@action Trip}. This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.
You bring the might of the mountain into your body. You cast 2nd-level or 4th-level {@spell enlarge} upon yourself. If you're at least 15th level, the duration increases to 1 hour.

footers.name: Epitome
entries: When you epitomize {@i The Mountain Man}, assign it to a point of interest in {@plane the harrow court|SF1|the Harrow Court's} mountains. This marks the location of a remote cabin that serves as the home of a self-sufficient but very intimidating simulacrum who appears as a towering giant of a man. This hearty specimen welcomes visitors who bring stories of their accomplishments fighting monsters, as long as they're backed up by physical trophies. A character who visits the mountain man and presents to him a trophy harvested from a monster they fought and defeated can seek a reward. The trophy need not be much more than a horn or a claw, but should be something significant and identifiable from the defeated monster, and the PC presenting the trophy must have been involved in that monster's defeat. If the trophy is from a monster whose level is equal to or greater than the PC's level, the mountain man is impressed and rewards that PC with two consumable magic items, each of a level equal to or lower than the PC's level (the PC can request specific items, but the GM has final say in what items are offered). If the trophy is from a monster whose level is lower than the PC's level, the mountain man mocks the PC for being "proud of defeating a weakling" and offers no reward. Once a reward is given, the mountain man warns the PC, "Now don't you be going off to sell that thing for gold, and don't even think of coming back for more rewards until you've used these all up!" The mountain man has an eerie ability to know if a PC hasn't used a current reward, or if they sold it for a profit—PCs who fit either category cannot receive new rewards from the mountain man on subsequent visits.

item.name: The Silent Hag
entries: {@i The Silent Hag} represents insight, treacherous secrets, and strife. As long as you have {@i The Silent Hag} invested, it grants you a +2 item bonus to {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Nature}, {@skill Occultism}, or {@skill Religion} checks to {@action Recall Knowledge}—when you invest the card, choose which of these four skills gains the bonus. You can change the skill by investing the card again. This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.
You choose to lose one of your senses and gain another until you use this activation again. Choose from one of the following:

items: Your eyes are replaced by dark pits that see only death. You become {@condition blinded} and gain {@ability lifesense}, an imprecise sense out to 60 feet. {@ability Lifesense} allows you to see the vital essence of living and {@trait undead} creatures, distinguishing between the positive energy animating living creatures and negative energy animating {@trait undead} creatures, much as sight distinguishes colors.
Your ears close up then become covered with hairs that are sensitive to movement. You become {@condition deafened}, but you can't be flanked.
Your mouth seals over with flesh. You lose the ability to speak, but you do not need to breathe.

footers.name: Epitome
entries: An unsettling statue of a crouching, eyeless hag with an open mouth manifests in a small chamber in Harrowheart. This mouth can accommodate most {@item crystal ball (generic)||crystal balls}. A {@item crystal ball (generic)||crystal ball} placed within the mouth is enhanced—its save DC increases by 1, its {@spell scrying} activation can be activated three times per day instead of twice per day, and its effects can extend beyond the planar borders of {@plane the Harrow Court|SF1} to target creatures on Golarion.

item.name: The Paladin
entries: {@i The Paladin} represents righteousness and resolute defense. As long as you have {@i The Paladin} invested, you gain the {@feat Shield Block} general feat. If you already possess this feat, you gain an additional reaction at the start of your turn that can only be used to {@feat Shield Block}.

entries.trigger: You fail or critically fail a saving throw
entries: Adjust the result of your saving throw up by one degree of success.

footers.name: Epitome
entries: A knighthood of paladins clad in shining armor manifests in the Harrow Court. In addition to providing additional defense to the demiplane (which will aid the PCs when {@plane the Harrow Court|SF1} is invaded in "The Destiny War"), the paladins can teach the PCs the formulas for {@item sturdy shield (generic)||sturdy shields}, {@item holy||holy weapon} runes, and {@item axiomatic||axiomatic weapon} runes.

item.name: The Publican
entries: {@i The Publican} represents friendship, shelter, and insight. As long as you have {@i The Publican} invested, treat critically failed checks made to {@action Aid} as regular failures instead. If you are at least 14th level, the circumstance bonus you provide for succeeding or critically succeeding at checks to {@action Aid} increases by 1.

entries.trigger: You improve a creature's attitude to you
entries: You improve the creature's attitude by an additional step more than you would normally. If you're at least 18th level, you improve the creature's attitude by two additional steps.

footers.name: Epitome
entries: A tavern appears in the village surrounding Harrowheart, run by a jovial one-eyed bartender. The tavern is always bustling with a rotating cast of different patrons and performers. The bartender knows the {@ritual heroes' feast|APG} ritual and can teach it to the PCs. Skill checks attempted at the tavern to perform this ritual gain a +2 item bonus. If {@i The Juggler} has been epitomized, and the town square is linked to a city, the patrons of this tavern trade gossip from that city as if they were citizens there, allowing a character to {@action Gather Information} in the tavern as if they were doing so on the streets of the linked city.

item.name: The Rabbit Prince
entries: {@i The Rabbit Prince} represents the unreliability of hand-to-hand combat, and how even cunning foes can lose to lucky novices. As long as you have {@i The Rabbit Prince} invested, it grants you a +1 status bonus to attack rolls you make as a {@action Ready||readied} action.

entries.trigger: You miss a creature with a melee weapon {@action Strike}
entries: Reroll the triggering {@action Strike} with a +1 status bonus. If you hit, attempt a DC {@flatDC 15} flat check; on a failure, your weapon gains the {@condition broken} condition (if your weapon is already {@condition broken}, it's destroyed). If you're at least 14th level, this flat check is DC {@flatDC 10}. If you're at least 17th level, this flat check is DC {@flatDC 5}.

footers.name: Epitome
entries: When you epitomize {@i The Rabbit Prince}, assign it to a point of interest within {@plane the harrow court|SF1|the Harrow Court's} forest area. This indicates a section of woodland where the simulacra of {@plane the Harrow Court|SF1} have reported sightings of an anthropomorphic rabbit. A PC can travel to this location and attempt to spot the elusive Rabbit Prince by spending 8 hours stealthily scouting the woods and attempting a DC 30 {@skill Stealth} check, after which no one may search for the Rabbit Prince again for 1 week.

Critical Success: You surprise the Rabbit Prince and he is impressed enough to gift you a +2 striking weapon. The specific type of weapon is up to you, but it must be a {@trait common} weapon. The Rabbit Prince is now on the lookout for your tricks, and you can never attempt this activity again.
Success: You spot the Rabbit Prince for a moment, but he doesn't spot you. The next time you perform this activity, you gain a +4 circumstance bonus to your {@skill Stealth} check.
Failure: You do not spot the Rabbit Prince.
Critical Failure: You don't spot the Rabbit Prince, but he spots you. He's insulted by your curiosity and triggers a trap that inflicts a serious wound upon you. You become {@condition clumsy||clumsy 3} for 1 week or until the condition is removed via an effect like {@spell restoration}.

item.name: The Rakshasa
entries: {@i The Rakshasa} represents domination of others to support your own schemes. When you invest {@i The Rakshasa}, identify a single willing creature within 30 feet as your pledged follower. If you're at least 15th level, you can have up to two pledged followers at once. At 18th level, you can have up to three pledged followers. If you have the maximum pledged followers active and select a new one, a previous pledged follower of your choice is no longer your pledged follower. You gain an item bonus equal to your current number of pledged followers to all {@action Coerce} attempts.

You regain Hit Points equal to twice your level, and a pledged follower of your choice loses Hit Points equal to your level (no effects apply that would decrease this Hit Point loss). If this loss kills your pledged follower, you also gain temporary Hit Points equal to your level. The pledged follower is temporarily immune to this activation for 24 hours.

footers.name: Epitome
entries: A simulacrum of a tiger-headed rakshasa moves into a decadent chamber in Harrowheart's basement. While sinister and prone to cruel comments, this rakshasa does not plot against the PCs and is content to idle away their time in their underground pleasure chambers. Once per day, a visitor to the rakshasa can pose them a question that they can use their {@skill Occultism} {@d20 +18} skill to attempt to {@action Recall Knowledge} about. The rakshasa also knows several {@trait uncommon} spells and rituals that they can teach spellcasters—these spells and rituals all involve the intrusive manipulation of sapient minds. Among the spells it can teach are {@spell dominate}, {@spell mind probe}, {@spell mind reading}, and {@spell modify memory}; rituals it can teach include {@ritual geas} and {@ritual inveigle}. Feel free to add similar spells to this list as you see fit.

item.name: The Snakebite
entries: {@i The Snakebite} represents poison, assassination, and disharmony. As long as you have {@i The Snakebite} invested, it grants you a +2 item bonus to {@skill Deception} and {@skill Stealth} checks you make for initiative. This increases to a +3 item bonus if you're at least 17th level. The DCs of your {@trait poison} effects have a +1 item bonus to targets that are {@condition flat-footed} to you when you afflict the target with the poison (the DC retains this bonus for the target's subsequent saves against the affliction, even if the target is no longer {@condition flat-footed} to you).
You cast {@spell purple worm sting} on a creature within your reach, with a DC equal to your class DC.

footers.name: Epitome
entries: When you epitomize {@i The Snakebite}, assign it to a point of interest in {@plane the harrow court|SF1|the Harrow Court's} swamp. This indicates a region of swampland that has become particularly infested with poisonous creatures and plants. A character who travels to this area can attempt a {@skill Crafting}, {@skill Lore||Herbalism Lore}, {@skill Lore||Swamp Lore}, or {@skill Lore||Underworld Lore} check to attempt to harvest some of their chosen poison from the region while spending 8 hours there. The DC of the check is equal to the poison's saving throw DC. Unlike most materials from {@plane the Harrow Court|SF1}, poison gathered from this part of the swamp continues to exist for 1 week before vanishing, even if it's brought out of {@plane the Harrow Court|SF1}.

Critical Success: The PC gathers 3 doses of the poison.
Success: The PC gathers 1 dose of the poison.
Failure: The PC fails to gather any poison.
Critical Failure: As failure, but the PC is also exposed to a dose of the poison they seek.

item.name: The Theatre
entries: {@i The Theater} represents prophecy and how prophets can't change the unfolding pageantry of fate. As long as you have {@i The Theater} invested and as long as you are not already {@condition doomed}, when you would gain the {@condition doomed} condition, attempt a DC {@flatDC 10} flat check. On a success, you do not gain the {@condition doomed} condition.

entries.trigger: You are targeted by a {@trait misfortune} effect
entries: {@i The Theater} attempts to counter the {@trait misfortune} effect before it affects you. It has a counteract level equal to your level divided by 2 (rounded up), and a counteract modifier of your Class DC − 10.

footers.name: Epitome
entries: A resplendent theater manifests in the village surrounding Harrowheart. Every evening, a talented troupe of actors puts on a new play that, with the PCs' permission, recounts a previous set of encounters they experienced. A PC who attends one of these two-hour productions benefits from the troupe's uncanny ability to recreate their exploits and receives a +2 item bonus to checks to {@action Recall Knowledge} about topics associated with these encounters.

item.name: The Trumpet
entries: {@i The Trumpet} represents timely warning. As long as you have {@i The Trumpet} invested, you (and only you) hear the sound of trumpets when you're about to be attacked. This grants you a +2 item bonus to initiative checks made with hearing-based {@skill Perception} checks. This bonus increases to +3 if you're at least 17th level.

A blast of inspiring noise erupts from the card in a 60-foot cone. Creatures in the area take {@damage 14d6} sonic damage (with a basic Fortitude save equal to your class DC). Creatures that fail the save are {@condition deafened} for 1 round (1 minute on a critical failure). The damage increases to {@damage 16d6} if you're at least 13th level, to {@damage 18d6} if you're at least 15th level, to {@damage 20d6} if you're at least 17th level, and to {@damage 22d6} if you're at least 19th level.

footers.name: Epitome
entries: Heralds outfitted with trumpets take up position on the battlements of Harrowheart. These heralds use their trumpets to raise the alarm should intruders enter {@plane the Harrow Court|SF1} (an event that won't happen in this adventure—but that shall in the next one!). The heralds know the formulas for all manner of magical instruments, including {@item horn of blasting||horns of blasting}, {@item horn of fog||horns of fog}, and {@item maestro's instrument (generic)||maestro's instruments}, and can teach these formulas to the PCs.

item.name: The Vision
entries: {@i The Vision} represents arcane knowledge. As long as you have {@i The Vision} invested, it grants you a +2 item bonus to all checks made to {@action Identify Magic}. This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.

A visible bolt of blue energy bursts from your head. Attempt to {@action Recall Knowledge} about a subject, rolling the check with the most appropriate {@skill Lore} skill check. This check always resolves as if you were master in the most appropriate {@skill Lore} skill to {@action Recall Knowledge} on the subject (or if you're at least 15th level, as if you were legendary in that {@skill Lore} skill). If you're already master (or legendary) in that {@skill Lore}, the result of your {@action Recall Knowledge} check is one degree of success better than it would otherwise be.

footers.name: Epitome
entries: Harrowheart's workshops become enhanced. Any character may now use a workshop in Harrowheart to attempt to {@action borrow an arcane spell||Borrow a Spell}, {@action Identify Alchemy}, {@action Identify Magic}, or {@action Learn a Spell}. If they do so, they apply the workshop's item bonus to their skill check.
